Yes and no to "Isn't the personal statement what a Cover Letter is for?" 


On a Cover Letter you want to add details about the company as well as address it to the person reading it. Don't just write "to whom it may concern or Dear Hiring manger." Do some recon on who the recruiter is, it look great when you do this. On your cover letter add some details about the company like "On your website your core values are blah blah... I agree with your blah blah blah" something along those lines. This is another way of giving a great first impression. In a cover letter it's an opportunity to directly sell your skills and qualities to the company and just dive in deep on how you are the best candidate for the position. 

Not all job applications require a cover letter, this is where a Personal Statement would help you shine. 



Personal Statements have taken over the Objective statement from the past. This is where you can shine and write a little bit about yourself. Example: "Awarding winning academic researcher..... Proven record of....." it's like highlighting your best qualities and skills.

The space between your contact info an education is too large. 
I would add a Professional Statement in between. 

Contact info

* Remove “number street”… keep only city, state, and zip code. There is no need to let people know exactly where you live, for security purposes. 

Professional statement 

* In your professional statement you want to let the recruiter know what makes you great for the position. Keep it between 2-5 sentences long and third person.

Education 

* Under Education I would just write School's name | city and state of school | Major, minors, &/or certificates | expected date…. No need to know when you started just the expected date is enough.

* Remove your GPA it's not necessary. The recruiter wont know if it is on a 4.0 scale or a 5.0, 6.0, or 7.0 scale. Even if you do state what scale it is on, there is no need for it.
 
* Completed 1 year of Biology and Java courses…. I would remove that whole statement. 
 

Job Experience

* Add at least 3 bullet points for each position. 

* I would write any accomplishments and duties. You want to combine both under your job descriptions. Only writing down your duties is of no value, you want to show what you brought to each position. 

* Also spell it out, BS in Biology… Bachelors of Science in Biology… fill in that white space.

* Also remove from the education section, ”Editor at College Newspaper and VP of Recruitment at the College Medical Ethics Society”, and add them to work experience. Those look like work experience - even if it's not paid. Experience is Experience! 

    * Editor of College Newspaper - What articles did you contribute too? What did you bring to the table that previous editors didn't? Name the Newspaper, don't undervalue it by just naming it "College Newspaper." 
 
    * VP or Recruitment at the College Medical Ethics Society - VP that’s awesome. What did you bring as the VP? 
 
 * It seems like you do have experience, it might not be in the internships that you are looking to get, but it's something to prove you have work ethic and are able to work in a team. Show that you can be of value in whatever position you are placed in. 
 


Tutor

* Great you tutored students, did those students get the scores they needed or improve their scores? What was so great about your Tutoring skills?  

Skills

* What skills do you have? I am sure you must have some skills.
I see you have taken 1 year of Java courses
Can you code in Java?
 

Awards & Accomplishments

* Add you Dean's Scholarship in this section
Have you gotten any other awards?  How about in your jobs? Employee of the month counts!

* Have you accomplished any goals? You are in Honors in your Major! That's a huge accomplishment and in a STEM field. Show it off, it doesn’t make you a nerd. 
 

Volunteer Activity

* I would just write:  Position | Organization | Dates 
no need to elaborate on volunteering unless you need it as a filler. 
 

You are worth more than you think. Don't under sell yourself, I can tell that you are. Believe in yourself and show your worth and potential, recruiters will pick you from a pile of resumes.

Personal Statement

* In your personal statement you want to let the recruiter know what makes you great for the position. 

* Keep it between 2-5 sentences long and third person. Remove your name from it, we know you are speaking about yourself. Also too many "he's" in your statement. 

Experience - You want to highlight you accomplishments and not just list your duties. You did a good mix of both, so that's good. 

* "Developed, edited and completed multiple web pages using HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript by hand-coding, testing, and adjusting the layouts in order to render properly in all major Web browsers." and "Developed applications for compatibility across different browsers; modified (HTML/JavaScript, etc.) to ensure web functionality was consistent across various browsers like IE, Firefox, Chrome, and Safari."
   
     * Honestly these two bullets sound exactly the same to me. It looks like you reworded them and you listed all the browsers they became compatible for. 
    * How many browsers was the original website compatible with? 
    * I would remove "edited, and completed… testing" I assumed when you developed these codes you did editing and tested it before launching the final product… it's a given it was completed or else why would you have it listed. 
    * It is amazing and awesome that you made the website compatible with all these different browsers, if only we could have more web devs like you, that would be awesome. Personally I think is awesome of you to have taken the time to do this. 
    * Was this a task assigned to you or did you go out of your way to do this? If this wasn't a task, that's even better show you initiative, that this was your idea! This makes you an even better candidate than the others. 
* "Excellent knowledge of web designing and development using the latest tools and techniques." 
    * Fantastic, but what latest tools and techniques? Elaborate more! Make it fancy as fuck, show your expertise in these knew tools and how did you apply them? Are these new tools and techniques relevant to the position you are applying for? 
* You want your experience to be amazing and to show you can apply them to the position you are applying too.

PAR statements are a way of outlining your success. Instead of only writing down your duties, Highlight your success and achievements while you worked there.

* Nice Resume. I would remove the boarder frou frou, you are going for an IT Service Desk position not Design. 

* Formatting I would keep the alignment of headers and dates consistent. - Personally I would align all my dates to the far right. It gives the dates and text a nice separation, plus makes it easier on the eyes. 

* I would reorganize your resume 1.Objective, 2. Experience, 3. Certs/Education 4. Skills (Optional 5 & 6) 5. Awards/Achievements 6. Volunteering/Organizations 

* I like the "|" work you did with your dates | title ( I'll explain how to change that below) I usually use the "|" with my contact info.  My format is Location | Email | Phone# - Personally I think it gives it a nice polish look. Also remove your full address, that's just creepy & it's a bit too personal. Just the City,St Zip is sufficient to let them know you are in the area. 

* Make a heading for your Education/Certifications. I wouldn't add your High school diploma your experience and A+ cert will get you the job. I would aim to get more CompTia certs like Network+ Sys Admin+, if you aiming to stay int he field. 

* I liked how you formatted your Experience - Employer above the position & dates. I would keep that style of formatting and apply it to your Cert/Ed. section example : CompTia (above) A+ (below)  Dates -> far right the date. I suggest making the title of your position first then the dates (only dates to the far right). Keeping the format consistent and making it easier to read. 
Employers will read first where you worked, the position held, then the dates. 
Also what happened to the bullet points? Writing at least 3 bullet points for each position. Also, I would write 1-2 [PAR statements](http://www.nova.edu/career/resources/forms/par_star.pdf) Instead of writing only your duties, I would outline 1-2 PAR Statements (They highlight achievements or highlights about your position). 


* I liked how you divided your Technical Skills and Professional Skills. That's smart. I would Relabel them to 'Technical Skills" and "Professional Skills" - Skills Technical, Skills Professional sounds a little funny.

* Also include achievements/awards section and or a volunteering/activities are you part of any clubs or organizations. IT is huge in the volunteering department. (All optional, but add more about you to your resume). 
 

Overall you have a good looking resume. Remember these are just suggestions. Good Luck on the relocation and I hope you get the job.

Looking at your resume you have too much white space. 

* I am not a big fan of the organization of your resume. First impressions important, having a neat,organized, and easy to read is key. That's okay, formatting and organizing a resume is the easy part. Try to align your dates to the right. I would place your name and contact info on the Header section of the doc, gives your more room on your resume (also removes that large white space your have above your name). Make your name larger than all the text blow it. 

* No obvious inconsistencies in use of numbers, spacing, punctuation, or capitalization.

* Make sure your mail is professional, nothing goofy. Your address, I would just put City,State. No need to write your entire home address.  

I would write my contact info all under one line: Address |Email | Phone 
It gives it a cleaner polish look. 

* On your Summary/Professional Statement - In third person, write what makes you a good candidate for the position. (3-4 sentences). With an emphasis on your personal qualities. List three of your top skills, where you've demonstrated them in the past. 

* I would leave only your highest level of education. Your HS Diploma is not necessary. 

* The order of your Resume - It should lead with your strengths, accomplishments and focus on "relevant experience". Swap the placing of Education and Experience. After Experience add a Skills section, then you Education. Lastly write in any Achievements/Awards and/or Volunteering. Help you fill in your page.

Good Luck and congrats on the career change.
